definitions.explanation: A formal speech delivered at a funeral or memorial service to honor and remember the deceased. In Japanese custom, the speaker typically addresses the deceased directly.

examples.japanese: {友人|ゆうじん}{代表|だいひょう}として{弔辞|ちょうじ}を{述|の}べた。
examples.english: I delivered a eulogy as the representative of the friends.

examples.japanese: {心|こころ}のこもった{弔辞|ちょうじ}に{参列者|さんれつしゃ}の{多|おお}くが{涙|なみだ}を{流|なが}した。
examples.english: Many of the attendees shed tears at the heartfelt eulogy.

notes:
A formal speech delivered at a funeral or memorial service to honor and remember the deceased. In Japanese funerals, the {弔辞|ちょうじ} is typically read from a prepared text written on special paper ({奉書紙|ほうしょがみ}), and the speaker usually addresses the deceased directly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弔辞|ちょうじ}を{読|よ}む: to read a eulogy
- {弔辞|ちょうじ}を{述|の}べる: to deliver a eulogy
- {弔辞|ちょうじ}を{依頼|いらい}する: to be asked to give a eulogy
- {心|こころ}のこもった{弔辞|ちょうじ}: a heartfelt eulogy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {追悼|ついとう}の{言葉|ことば}: words of condolence/remembrance — a less formal way to describe memorial remarks
- {弔電|ちょうでん}: condolence telegram — a written message of sympathy sent to a funeral
- {祝辞|しゅくじ}: congratulatory speech — the opposite occasion; a speech at a celebration
